items.t: What Is Drawing Fresh Attention To CNOOC (SEHK:883)?
sum: CNOOC (SEHK:883) drew fresh attention on 30 October 2026 after reporting third quarter and year to date production alongside nine month earnings, with both output volumes and net income higher than a year earlier.

At a share price of HK$23.48, CNOOC has had a mixed few months, with the 1 day share price return of 0.86% and a year to date share price gain of 7.41% sitting alongside recent 7 day weakness. The 1 year total shareholder return of 17.58% and very strong 3 and 5 year total shareholder returns point to momentum that has been building over a longer horizon as investors respond to improving production and earnings trends.

Bulls point to CNOOC's rising production, stronger nine month earnings and long run shareholder gains, while bears focus on recent share price softness. Which case does the current valuation support next?

CNOOC's widely followed thesis places fair value at about HK$31.77, comfortably above the HK$23.48 last close. This frames the current debate around how durable its cash generation and project pipeline really are.

Robust investment in reserve expansion and accelerated project development, supported by recent discoveries of four new oil and gas structures and the appraisal of 16 prospects together with new projects such as Kenli 10-2, Yellowtail in Guyana and Buzios 8 in Brazil, supports the view that CNOOC can extend production growth through 2030 and sustain revenue and earnings.
Still, the story can break if CNOOC faces tighter geopolitical restrictions on overseas projects, or if policy and energy transition pressures weaken long term oil demand.
With CNOOC described as 26% undervalued by this thesis and sentiment split, move quickly to check the data yourself and weigh both sides using the 3 key rewards and 2 important warning signs.

PetroChina Shares Hit 18-Year High as Middle East War Fears Lift Oil Majors
sum: PetroChina Co. (601857.SS) climbed to its highest level in more than 18 years on Monday, leading a broad rally across China's state-owned oil giants as escalating Middle East hostilities kept crude prices near six-month peaks.

The stock touched 13.41 yuan intraday, a level last seen in May 2008 on an adjusted basis, before closing up 4.94% at 13.38 yuan. That leaves the shares roughly 54% above their late-June low. China Petroleum & Chemical Corp., or Sinopec (600028.SS), added 3.54% to 5.56 yuan, while CNOOC Ltd. (600938.SS) gained 4.27% to 35.16 yuan.

The gains rippled through the oil-services chain: China Oilfield Services Ltd. (601808.SS) rose more than 7%, Offshore Oil Engineering Co. (600583.SS) advanced nearly 6% and CNOOC Energy Technology & Services Ltd. (600968.SS) added over 4%.
Hong Kong-listed units tracked the move. PetroChina (0857.HK) jumped 5.78% to lead blue-chip gainers on the Hang Seng Index, Sinopec (0386.HK) rose 4.04% and CNOOC Ltd. (0883.HK) climbed 3.55%.

The rally has been building since late February, when the US and Israel opened a war with Iran aimed at ending its nuclear program. On March 2, all three of China's flagship state oil companies closed limit-up on the same day for the first time on record, and repeated the feat the following session.

Crude benchmarks retreated modestly on Monday after last week's surge. December Brent futures fell 1.1% to $115.40 a barrel in Asian trading, and US West Texas Intermediate dropped 1.4% to $101.88. Brent had settled at $116.72 on Friday, its highest close since April 29, and gained about 6% for the week; WTI settled at $103.27, up 2.3% weekly.

The pullback followed a warning from a technical gauge: Brent's 14-day relative-strength index exceeded 74 on Friday, above the 70 threshold that some traders read as a signal of overbought conditions.

CNOOC Stock Technicals: Drops 1.03% on Friday, Testing Support Level
sum: On October 23, 2026: price 23.12 HKD, trend sideways, RSI 39.2, support 23.12, resistance 24.72. technical analysis of cnooc stock. CNOOC Stock Technicals —…

CNOOC Limited closed at HK$23.12, its lowest level in the past 20 trading days, while its MACD histogram has just turned negative. The stock fell 1.03% on the day and 4.46% over five days, putting short-term pressure on a share price that is already below both key moving averages. The decline came with trading volume at 1.3 times its 20-day average. That makes the latest weakness harder to dismiss as a low-participation move.

At HK$23.12, CNOOC is below its SMA20 of HK$23.82 and SMA50 of HK$24.31. The SMA20 is nearly flat, rising just 0.03% over five days, so the broader technical picture is sideways rather than a firmly established downtrend. But the share price sitting beneath both averages indicates that sellers currently have the upper hand: those averages may act as overhead resistance if the stock attempts to recover.

There has been no recent moving-average crossover to signal a decisive change in trend. Instead, the price has reached the lower edge of its 20-day range, with HK$23.12 support and HK$24.72 resistance. The three-month range, from HK$22.52 to HK$26.00, places the current price closer to its low than its high.
As shown in the chart, the price is also near the lower Bollinger Band. This can mark a stretched decline, but it does not by itself confirm that a rebound has begun.

The indicators present a mixed picture. RSI at 39.2 is neutral, below the level that would usually indicate strong positive momentum but not, on its own, an oversold reading. The Stochastic oscillator is more stretched: %K at 13.3 and %D at 25.5 are in oversold territory, suggesting the recent selling has been pronounced. Oversold conditions can precede a bounce, yet they can also persist while a share price remains weak.

The MACD adds a cautionary signal. MACD is -0.136, below its -0.092 signal line, with a -0.044 histogram, showing negative momentum. The histogram’s turn below zero is especially relevant because it indicates that the balance of short-term momentum has shifted lower. A sustained improvement would require that pressure to ease, not merely a low Stochastic reading.

items.t: Hong Kong Stock Market Today, September 8, 2026: Hang Seng Falls 0.5% To 25,283 As Oil Prices Rise, Check Why Hong Kong Stocks Are Falling And Key Stocks To Watch
sum: Hong Kong equities remained under pressure on Tuesday, with the Hang Seng Index declining for a second straight session. The benchmark fell around 0.5% to 25,283, as investors remained cautious amid higher oil prices and ongoing geopolitical concerns. The rise in energy costs has raised worries about renewed inflationary pressure, potentially making it harder for central banks to reduce interest rates. Investors were also awaiting China’s August trade figures for clues about the strength of the world’s second-largest economy.

Market sentiment was affected by concerns that elevated oil prices could keep inflation higher for longer. This could limit the scope for global central banks to cut borrowing costs. Technology stocks were among the weaker performers. Xiaomi fell around 2.1% in the latest market data, while Tencent Holdings was broadly unchanged and Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing declined 0.4%.
Other major stocks showed mixed movement, with HSBC Holdings down 0.84% and China Construction Bank losing 0.68%. In contrast, CNOOC gained 2.89%, benefiting from strength in the energy sector.
The broader Chinese market was relatively steadier compared with Hong Kong.
The figures indicate that mainland Chinese equities were holding up better than Hong Kong stocks during the session.

Technology companies remained a key area of weakness in Hong Kong. Xiaomi was among the notable decliners, while Tencent and Meituan also faced pressure during the session. The weakness in technology shares contributed to the broader decline in the Hang Seng.
Investors are closely watching the sector amid concerns over valuations, economic growth and the impact of global trade conditions on Chinese companies.

Latest Personnel Changes at CNOOC's Two Listed Companies: Zhou Tianyu and Shang Jie Assume Important New Posts
sum: Recently, CNOOC Energy Technology Co., Ltd. (stock abbreviation: CNOOC Energy Tech, 600968) and China Oilfield Services Limited (stock abbreviation: COSL, 601808), both subsidiaries of China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC), successively released information regarding personnel appointments and dismissals. The core management teams of both companies have undergone significant adjustments, laying a solid foundation for the management structure to support future business development and operations.
CNOOC Energy Tech: Zhou Tianyu appointed as Party Secretary and Chairman

Following organizational appointments, Zhou Tianyu, former Deputy Party Secretary and General Manager of CNOOC Energy Tech, has officially been promoted to Party Secretary and Chairman of CNOOC Energy Technology Co., Ltd.

Public records show that Zhou Tianyu, of Chinese nationality, was born in 1974. He graduated from Southwest Petroleum University in 1997 with a bachelor's degree in engineering in Petroleum Engineering (Oil Production). In 2007, he obtained a master's degree in engineering in Petroleum and Natural Gas Engineering from Southwest Petroleum University. Having joined the CNOOC system in 1997, he has worked extensively in frontline offshore oil production, human resource management, and regional Party affairs management, possessing rich experience in frontline operations of the oil and gas industry as well as management at the group headquarters.

In terms of career history, Zhou Tianyu has successively served as General Manager of the Wenchang Oilfield Operating Company of the Zhanjiang Branch of CNOOC China Limited, Manager of the Human Resources Department of the Zhanjiang Branch, Deputy Secretary of the Party Working Committee of the Western South China Sea Region, Deputy Party Secretary, Chairman of the Labor Union, and Deputy Secretary of the Regional Party Working Committee for the Zhanjiang and Hainan Branches, Deputy General Manager of the Human Resources Department of CNOOC Group, and Deputy Party Secretary and General Manager of CNOOC Energy Tech.

items.t: CNOOC upgrades automation systems at Buzzard North Sea oil field
sum: (WO) — ABB has been awarded a contract to modernize automation and safety control systems on the Buzzard offshore platform, supporting continued operations at one of the UK's largest producing oil fields in the North Sea.

The project, awarded by CNOOC Petroleum Europe Limited, will upgrade ABB's existing System 800xA distributed control system and Safeguard 400 safety system installed on the platform. The phased modernization program is designed to improve operational resilience while allowing the facility to remain online during the upgrade process.
Buzzard is located approximately 100 km northeast of Aberdeen and is one of the cornerstone assets in the UK North Sea.
ABB said the phased approach will minimize production disruptions and reduce project risk by introducing system updates while maintaining ongoing operations.
The work will be managed by ABB's Aberdeen-based engineering team, which supports the platform through an onshore reference system used to test and validate upgrades before deployment offshore.

“This project reflects our longstanding partnership with CNOOC's UK business and our shared commitment to safe and reliable operations,” said Nicolas Alonso, head of ABB's Energy Industries division for the UK, Ireland and Azerbaijan. “By modernizing the existing automation systems, we are able to help support UK energy security at a time of increasing demand.”
According to ABB, testing upgrades onshore before installation offshore will help reduce operational risk, minimize downtime and maintain continuity of production.

ExxonMobil and Chevron Reported a Combined $7.6 Billion Profit in Guyana Last Year. What Energy Investors Need to Know.
sum: Amid growing concerns about the reliability of oil supplies due to heightened tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, the strength and durability of multinational oil companies have come under scrutiny.

ExxonMobil (XOM +0.34%) announced yesterday that its operations in Guyana generated $4.7 billion in profit last year, highlighting the significance of the South American nation’s offshore oil boom as a buffer against the geopolitical crisis in the Middle East.

Incidentally, another supermajor, Chevron (CVX -0.15%), through its acquisition of Hess, had disclosed a $2.89 billion profit in 2025 from Guyana. It’s no secret that oil companies and investors are looking to diversify their energy investments away from any single region.

At 6.6 million acres, the Stabroek block is a giant, low-cost, high-margin oil discovery located in deepwater territory. While ExxonMobil has a 45% working interest, Chevron has a 30% interest through Hess. The Chinese state-owned oil company CNOOC holds the remaining 25%.
Since ExxonMobil discovered this oilfield in 2015, the consortium has identified more than 11 billion barrels of recoverable oil, making it the largest crude oil discovery over the last decade.

What sets Stabroek apart is its economics. On some projects, including ExxonMobil's Yellowtail development, breakeven costs are as low as $25 per barrel, far below the global average and roughly half the onshore breakeven of many U.S. shale plays. EBITDA margins for ExxonMobil Guyana Limited hit 58% in 2024.
It’s difficult to dispute these numbers in an era when big oil's critics argue the sector faces structural decline.

items.t: US adds BYD, Nio and battery maker CALB to Chinese military company blacklist
sum: The US Department of Defence has added several Chinese EV makers, battery makers, and technology companies to its list of “Chinese military companies,” including BYD, Nio, and CALB.

The updated Section 1260H list also includes Alibaba, Baidu, battery maker EVE Energy, lidar makers Hesai and BYD-backed Robosense, WuXi AppTec, TP-Link, and robotic startup Unitree, according to a Federal Register notice scheduled for publication this week.
Nvidia announced a partnership with Unitree at the beginning of June. Eve Energy supplies batteries to Tesla, BMW, and Mercedes-Benz.

The Defence Department also removed several entities from the previous version of the list, including CNOOC China Ltd and CNOOC International Trading, both linked to China National Offshore Oil Corporation.

The Pentagon’s move does not automatically impose sanctions. However, it can restrict future US government procurement and may complicate business with US partners, especially in sectors connected to defence supply chains, capital markets, and government contracts. Companies on the list can petition the Pentagon for removal.

The Pentagon said BYD is directly and indirectly affiliated with China’s State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC) and indirectly affiliated with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT). It also claimed that BYD is a “military-civil fusion contributor” because of its links to MIIT and its location in, or affiliation with, a military-civil fusion enterprise zone, according to a Department of Defence document viewed by CarNewsChina.
For Nio, the Pentagon said the EV maker is directly and indirectly affiliated with SASAC and is a military-civil fusion contributor because it is affiliated with MIIT.

items.t: New Forecasts: Here's What Analysts Think The Future Holds For CNOOC Limited (HKG:883)
sum: Shareholders in CNOOC Limited (HKG:883) may be thrilled to learn that the analysts have just delivered a major upgrade to their near-term forecasts. The analysts greatly increased their revenue estimates, suggesting a stark improvement in business fundamentals.

Following the upgrade, the latest consensus from CNOOC's 15 analysts is for revenues of CN¥482b in 2026, which would reflect a sizeable 21% improvement in sales compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are presumed to bounce 33% to CN¥3.43. Prior to this update, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of CN¥413b and earnings per share (EPS) of CN¥2.77 in 2026. There has definitely been an improvement in perception recently, with the analysts substantially increasing both their earnings and revenue estimates.

It will come as no surprise to learn that the analysts have increased their price target for CNOOC 16% to CN¥27.54 on the back of these upgrades. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. The most optimistic CNOOC analyst has a price target of CN¥40.59 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at CN¥10.91. As you can see the range of estimates is wide, with the lowest valuation coming in at less than half the most bullish estimate, suggesting there are some strongly diverging views on how think this business will perform. With this in mind, we wouldn't rely too heavily on the consensus price target, as it is just an average and analysts clearly have some deeply divergent views on the business.

These estimates are interesting, but it can be useful to paint some more broad strokes when seeing how forecasts compare, both to the CNOOC's past performance and to peers in the same industry. The analysts are definitely expecting CNOOC's growth to accelerate, with the forecast 21% annualised growth to the end of 2026 ranking favourably alongside historical growth of 15% per annum over the past five years. Compare this with other companies in the same industry, which are forecast to grow their revenue 1.9% annually.

items.t: Black Monday hits Hong Kong stocks on Middle East turmoil, Hang Seng Index loses nearly 900 points
sum: Hong Kong stocks plunged on Monday, pressured by higher oil prices amid the expected prolonged Middle East war.
The benchmark Hang Seng Index once dived over 1,000 points before closing 894 points lower, or 3.54 percent to 24,382, the worst performance in nearly a year.
The full-day turnover rose to HK$368.6 billion, marking a two-week high.
Laopu Gold's (6181) shares dived 8.6 percent following the plunging gold prices, becoming the worst performer among blue chips.
Zijin Mining (2899) also slumped nearly 5 percent, after it said it plans to acquire the controlling power in Chifeng Gold (6693), with the latter diving 25.1 percent.
Oil majors delivered mixed performance. While CNOOC (0883) kept rising by 0.4 percent to a record high, PetroChina (0857) and Sinopec (0386) fell 1.4 percent and 3.2 percent, respectively.
Insurers' shares broadly went down. AIA (1299) sank 7.79 percent after it unveiled plans to issue US$18 billion (HK$141 billion) in debt, hitting a three-month low.

items.t: With higher prices, Guyana could get larger share of profits sooner – Routledge
sum: ExxonMobil could recover its historic investments in Guyana sooner as production grows and oil prices rise, potentially paving the way for the South American nation to receive a larger share of the profits by the end of 2026.
This is according to President of ExxonMobil Guyana, Alistair Routledge, who spoke at a press conference at the company’s Ogle headquarters on Thursday.

“While we’ve been generally running down that historical bank of costs at a reasonably steady and predictable pace, we were anticipating sometime next year, in 2027, that we were going to get to a point where we would have recovered those costs.

“… What we’re now seeing in this price environment is that it will accelerate. We don’t forecast oil prices, but if you stay at the current oil price, then it will happen this year, based on the level of expenditures and the production that we anticipate,” Routledge told reporters.
Oil prices have soared in recent weeks owing to the conflict in the Middle East.

ExxonMobil has been producing oil in Guyana’s giant Stabroek Block since December 2019. There are four current projects, producing more than 900,000 barrels of oil daily, and plans are afoot to initiate at least three others this decade.
Through its agreement with the Government of Guyana, ExxonMobil has been recovering the investments made. It has committed about US$60 billion, but not all of that has been spent yet.

Hang Seng Index crashes to key support level: will it hit H$20,000?
sum: The Hang Seng Index retreated by over 2% on Monday as Asian stocks dived amid the ongoing energy market shock. It retreated to a low of H$25,100, an important support level that was much lower than the year-to-date high of $28,000.
Chinese stocks continued falling on Monday, with the China A50 and Shanghai Composite falling by over 2%. Asian indices like the Nikkei 225,Nifty 50, and Kospi dropped by over 5%.

The same trend happened in Europe, where futures tied to the FTSE 100, DAX, and CAC 40 indices dropped by over 2%. Similarly, Dow Jones, Nasdaq 100, and S&P 500 futures dropped by over 2%, their worst performance in months.

The Hang Seng Index is falling because of the ongoing crisis in the Middle East, which has pushed energy prices substantially higher in the past few months. Brent, the global benchmark, was trading at $116, while the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose to $115.

Hong Kong and mainland China are exposed to the developments in the Middle East because of the vast amount of oil they import from the region. On the positive side, China has millions of barrels of oil in storage, which explains why its indices are falling at a slower margin than its counterparts.

The Hang Seng Index also retreated as investors watched the developments at the ongoing developments at the National People's Congress (NPC), where officials are sharing their plans for the year. In a statement last week, Beijing placed a target growth for the year to between 4.5% and 5%.

Most Hang Seng Index companies were in the red. The Sun Hung Kai Properties stock price dropped by 6.55% on Monday, while Techtronic fell by 6.22%. Geely Automobile, Hang Lung Properties, CITIC, CK Hutchinson, AIA Group, and Zijin Mining stocks tumbled by over 5%.

This upstream focus allows it to capture the upside from rising oil prices almost immediately.

China deploys large-scale drone operations in offshore oilfields
sum: BEIJING - China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) has launched a large-scale drone operation project, the first of its kind in the country, in the Beibu Gulf oilfields in South China, marking a pioneering step in integrating marine energy development with low-altitude economic activities.

The project has been rolled out across 41 offshore platforms and two onshore terminal plants in the Beibu Gulf, establishing a comprehensive drone operation system that covers subsea pipeline inspections, logistics delivery and emergency security responses, Science and Technology Daily reported on Monday.

These operational drones can now conduct rapid aerial inspections of over 500 kilometers of subsea pipelines, efficiently identifying anomalies such as leaks and initiating emergency protocols. They can also assist in search and rescue operations for vessels adrift and personnel that have fallen overboard.

According to Meng Wenbo, coordination manager at CNOOC's Zhanjiang branch in South China's Guangdong province, this low-altitude economy application has completed more than 3,600 kilometers of drone patrols and small-item logistics operations.

Notably, by replacing tugboats and helicopters with an air courier system, the company can save nearly 15 million yuan ($2.17 million) annually in vessel rental and fuel costs, while reducing carbon emissions by 25,000 tonnes, Meng said, adding that this option effectively lowers costs, improves efficiency, and supports the intelligent upgrade of offshore oil operations.

CNOOC, one of China's major offshore oil and gas exploration enterprises, has developed a customized "air-sea integrated" intelligent operation platform and standardized management processes for its drone operation systems.

items.t: Kenya Floats Biggest IPO Ever in High-Stakes Bet on Energy Infrastructure
sum: Kenya this week launched its biggest-ever initial public offering, the first share sale in 11 years, as it looks to list 65% of its state-owned pipeline company to raise funds for expanding energy infrastructure.

Kenya Pipeline Company (KPC) expects to raise $824 million (106.3 billion Kenyan shillings) by selling 11.81 billion shares to domestic and international investors and company employees in the IPO launched on January 19 and running until February 19.
Once listed, KPC is expected to be the fifth largest firm on the Nairobi Stock Exchange in terms of market capitalization.
The proceeds from the share sale will be used by the Kenyan government to fund infrastructure projects, including energy projects, while KPC will not keep any proceeds.

Kenya has been struggling with soaring debt in recent years and has resorted to programs and financing facilities from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). A previous $3.6 billion program with the IMF expired last year, and the country is in talks for additional IMF support that could help relieve its debt burden.

Against this backdrop, it is no surprise that the government is listing 65% of Kenya Pipeline Company, a key state-controlled asset that operates 1,342 kilometers, or 834 miles, of pipelines in the country, connecting the coastal city of Mombasa in the southeast to the interior. KPC also operates refineries, laboratory services, and fiber optic cables.

The company plans capital expenditure of $852 million (110 billion shillings) for the period to 2030, it said in its IPO prospectus. That’s triple the total investment between 2021 and 2025 as KPC looks to expand its pipeline network and build crude and LPG storage facilities.

sum: A ‘glut’ of new LNG supply from the US and Qatar is set to hit Asian markets
[SINGAPORE] The US “shale revolution” is about to export a windfall to Singapore, helping to defray the cost of powering the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.

A “glut” of new liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply from the US and Qatar is set to hit Asian markets, said a Morgan Stanley report on Jan 13, driving prices down by nearly half to around US$7 per million British thermal units (mmbtu) by 2027.
This supply glut arrives just as Singapore and its Asean neighbours face a critical surge in electricity demand from data centres and AI hyperscalers.
In Singapore, where 92 per cent of electricity is generated from natural gas, the impact will be two-fold: drastically reduced energy import bills and a fresh tailwind for its utilities sector.

“It should fundamentally change energy consumption dynamics, as the region imports half of its natural gas requirements,” said the analysts, noting that lower prices will help solve “grid bottlenecks and shortages in energy systems”.
Price-sensitive consumer markets will be the biggest beneficiaries of this affordable LNG, they added, highlighting India, followed by China, Japan and Vietnam, and then Singapore and Thailand.

items.t: China's $468 Billion Energy Drive Sparks Global Oil Market Shakeup
sum: A month ago, Chinese oil heavyweight CNOOC boasted its pipeline network had hit 10,000 kilometers. That network was going to further grow to 13,000 km, the company said soon after it announced a fresh offshore discovery in the South China Sea. What CNOOC is doing is what all Chinese oil majors are doing: ramping up domestic supply of oil and gas. It is the safest kind of supply.

Chinese state energy companies have spent some $468 billion on exploration and production since 2019, Bloomberg reported earlier this month, noting that the amount was 25% higher than E&P spending in the previous six months. It was, in fact, enough to make PetroChina the biggest investor in exploration and production globally, Bloomberg wrote—and there is a very good reason for this.

State-owned oil giants Sinopec, PetroChina, and CNOOC recently suspended purchases of Russian oil, at least in the short term, until the sanctions situation and implications become clearer, media reported following Washington’s decision to make a new attempt to squeeze Russian oil revenues by sanctioning two of the biggest exporters directly. Takers en route to Chinese ports were turning back, reports said, and orders were being canceled.

China’s crude oil imports in October averaged 11.4 million barrels daily, down slightly from the 11.5 million barrels daily in September but still higher than a year ago. Indeed, after a slow start to the year, China has been importing crude oil at elevated rates even as the immediate demand for the commodity remained weaker than in previous years for much of the year. There was one driver behind those higher import rates: stock-building.

China has crude oil inventories that analysts estimate at between 1.2 billion and 1.3 billion barrels. It has been building them at a rate of close to one million barrels daily. It is also building new storage capacity, meaning it would continue building its oil stocks in the future as well. At a planned 169 million barrels in total, the new storage capacity will be built this year and next, and compares with some 180-190 million barrels in new storage space built between 2020 and 2024.
